results.note: The same method reproduces IWB's published prices with VAT. What a private household pays.

how big is the water tank.query: how big is the water tank

results.label: Usable capacity of the heat storage tank
results.note: 1,000 kg × 4.186 kJ/kgK × 30 K = 34.9 kWh; the case value 35 is used.

results.label: Forecast horizon
results.note: A two-day horizon is shown as a sensitivity: the 35 kWh tank, not the forecast, limits how much reserve can be held.

results.label: Reference scheduling policy
results.note: Keeps only the heat reserve the forecast asks for, so the tank has room for deadline work.

results.label: Hot-water demand
Standby heat loss of the tank
results.note: A realistic loss is shown as a sensitivity.

how long may a job wait.query: how long may a job wait

results.label: A contracted job can be split across servers and paused at any hour
results.note: A job of 48 server-hours may use all 8 servers in the same hour. Switching a server on or off costs no time and no work; a real cold start takes about 4 minutes (2.5 to 8).

results.label: Completion window of a contracted job
results.note: Work delivered inside the window is paid; the rest is cancelled and the job counts as missed. 12 and 48 hours are shown as sensitivities.

results.label: Interruptible filler work
results.note: Filler has no deadline and buys every server-hour the house can use as heat.

results.label: Contracted batch jobs arriving per day and house
results.note: Missed deadlines rise steeply with this number; the Jobs page shows 3, 6, 12 and 24 jobs a day.

results.label: Deadline work may run even when its heat has to be dumped
results.note: With false, a contracted job that is due waits when house and tank are full, and may miss its deadline. Every missed deadline of the reference comes from this rule. The opposite choice is shown on the Method page.

results.label: Refurbished previous-generation 2-socket server (2x Xeon Gold 6138, 384 GB)
results.unit: CHF per server, landed in Switzerland
results.note: Base units were out of stock on the day read; shipping of about CHF 130 is assumed.

results.label: Price of contracted batch work (modern 1 kW server)
results.note: A judgement, not a quoted price. A single basement host without a service agreement can hardly charge more than a data-centre provider's hourly rate. Whether a buyer contracts such a host at all is a separate question the model does not answer. 1 kW of the new servers on the Money page has about 300 threads; the price is not scaled up for that, so it leans low.

results.label: Price of interruptible filler work (modern 1 kW server)
results.note: What hosts are paid on such marketplaces is not published and can be zero. 1 kW of the new servers on the Money page has about 300 threads; the price is not scaled up for that, so it leans low.

answers.label: How a heat pump works
answers.prompt: Explain in two sentences how a heat pump heats a house.
answers.text: A heat pump heats a house by transferring heat from a colder reservoir (like outside air) to a warmer reservoir (like inside the house), using a refrigerant to move heat between them.

answers.label: Summarise the idea
answers.prompt: Summarise in one sentence: Small servers in the basement of a house do computing jobs for paying customers. Their waste heat goes into the house's heating and hot water. A scheduler runs the jobs when the house needs heat and pauses them when it does not.
answers.text: Small servers in the basement of a house compute jobs for paying customers, with their waste heat helping to heat and supply hot water, and a scheduler manages the tasks based on when the house needs energy.

answers.label: Reasons to pause a job
answers.prompt: Give three short reasons why a computing job might be paused.
answers.text:
1. **Technical issues** may cause the system to stop functioning.  
2. **Unexpected errors** in the software or hardware can lead to a pause.  
3. **User requests** or system notifications may trigger a pause.

answers.label: A short poem
answers.prompt: Write a four-line poem about a server that heats a house.
answers.text:
The server hums with warmth,  
Heating the house with its light.  
Its coils dance, a steady glow,  
A sanctuary where the night is gone.
